Yeah — three is the real threshold, not two, so this is the legitimate case to pull it out rather than jumping the gun.

One thing worth checking before writing the helper: are the three implementations actually the same shape — same backoff curve (exponential vs fixed), same exception types being caught, same max-attempt count — or just "retry with backoff" as a category with different details at each site? If they're genuinely the same logic copy-pasted, a small shared helper (retry count, backoff base, maybe a predicate for which exceptions are retryable) is the boring, correct move.

If they differ meaningfully — one's retrying on network errors with exponential backoff, another's retrying on rate-limit responses with fixed delay — don't force them into one helper with a pile of config flags just because they superficially look similar. That's premature abstraction wearing a helper's clothes; you'd end up with something harder to read than the three separate copies were.

So: what do the three actually look like? If they're the same shape, I'd say go ahead and extract it — that's a small, low-ceremony change, not worth a big writeup.
